sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 of the 1909 Sanborn coverage of Cape May Point (New Jersey coast map series, volume 4), drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. It shows the northern and central part of the borough, from the Delaware Bay and Atlantic Ocean shore at the upper left and left edge across to Ocean Avenue and West Lake Drive on the right and bottom. The street plan radiates from the Pavilion, a circular park at the centre, with Cape, Pavilion, Ocean and Central Avenues leading out of it; to the north-west a grid of avenues named for gems (Beach, Emerald, Diamond, Crystal, Pearl) and to the north-east Brainard, Stites, Knox and Alexander Avenues, and along the bottom the college-named avenues Lincoln, Yale, Princeton, Cambridge and Oxford. Building is light and almost entirely frame dwellings and cottages on large numbered lots, many lots still empty. Named buildings include The Carlton hotel with its bath houses on Surf Avenue, the Beadle Presbyterian Church on Emerald Avenue, the Union Church and St. Agnes R.C. Church at the Pavilion, Floral Villa and Wright's Villa boarding houses on Cape Avenue, the Minola Rest, the Seaside Home for Women and Children near the bay, a school house on Cambridge Avenue, the street railway station on Lincoln Avenue, and the United Brethren Camp Meeting Ground with its hall and cottages between Stites and Knox Avenues. A trolley right of way crosses the upper part of the sheet toward the car barn shown on sheet 3. The shore, Beach Avenue and the blocks along it have since been lost to erosion.
notes: Central Avenue west of the Pavilion is today's West Central Avenue; Central Avenue south-east of it is East Central Avenue.
Beach, Emerald and Diamond Avenues and the shore blocks west of Lincoln Avenue (The Carlton, the Beadle Presbyterian Church) are lost to erosion and absent from modern data.
Ocean Avenue was left out of the control: on both sheets its modern line sits 2 to 5 m off the drawn street.
The upper part of today's Crystal Avenue follows the old trolley right of way.
The lake is lettered Lake Lilly on this sheet and Lake Lily on sheet 3.

Printed sheet 2 of N.J. coast map vol. 4, 100 ft to an inch, north about 57 deg clockwise (arrow at upper left agrees). One part: Cape May Point from Delaware Bay / Beach Av (eroded, not in modern data) east to Ocean Av and W. Lake Drive, centred on the Pavilion circle; Cape, Lincoln, Yale, Pearl, Central, Brainard, Stites, Knox, Alexander, Ocean, Princeton, Cambridge, Oxford Avs. Beach, Emerald and Diamond Avs and the blocks west of Lincoln Av (The Carlton) are lost to erosion.

sheet-3-1.description: Main part of sheet 3 of the 1909 Sanborn coverage of Cape May Point (New Jersey coast map series, volume 4), drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. It covers the southern part of the borough between the Atlantic Ocean and its board walk on the left and Lake Lily and Oxford Avenue on the right, from Surf and Ocean Avenues at the top down to Light House Avenue and the light house grounds at the bottom. The streets form a regular grid: Beach, Harvard, Lincoln, Yale, Princeton, Cambridge and Oxford Avenues running down the sheet, crossed by Lake Drive, Coral, Whilldin and Lehigh Avenues, with Light House Avenue running diagonally beside the trolley right of way toward the light house. Most lots are vacant; the scattered buildings are frame dwellings. Named buildings include St. Peter's by the Sea church on Ocean Avenue, The Shoreham Hotel (vacant) on Lehigh Avenue, the Cape May Point Water Works (for summer use only), the Cape May Light House with its keepers' dwellings, and the U. S. Life Saving Station south of Light House Avenue. A pond lies east of Light House Avenue. The lower right corner of the sheet holds a separate inset of the Delaware Bay shore, which is not part of this annotation. Beach Avenue, the blocks along it and Light House Avenue west of the trolley right of way have since been lost to erosion.
notes: Lake Drive between Harvard and Yale Avenues is today's South Lake Drive.
Beach Avenue, the board walk and the ocean blocks, and Light House Avenue west of the trolley right of way, are lost to erosion.
Ocean Avenue and the diagonal Light House Avenue were left out of the control: their modern lines sit 4 to 10 m off the drawn streets.
The inset at the lower right (Cape May Sand Co., Delaware Bay House, car barn) was not georeferenced.

Printed sheet 3, 100 ft to an inch, north about 58 deg clockwise. Part 1: main map from Surf Av / Ocean Av south to Light House Av and the light house, Harvard, Lincoln, Yale, Princeton, Cambridge, Oxford Avs, Lake Drive, Coral, Whilldin, Lehigh Avs; Beach Av and Light House Av west of the trolley right of way are eroded. Part 2: inset at lower right (north up) of the Delaware Bay shore with Cape May Sand Co., Delaware Bay House and the car barn (about 800 ft from Alexander Av); no streets drawn.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Cape May Sand Co., Delaware Bay House and trolley car barn on the Delaware Bay shore (no street or other surviving feature drawn; the shore has moved; needs hand-picked control from a dated aerial or a surviving building; none identified).
